rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A detailed study of Pinus (gymnosperm) reveals a woody plant with needle-like leaves and cones. The male cone bears microsporangia that produce pollen grains (each with a body and an air-sac for wind dispersal). The female cone bears the ovule on the cone scale; pollination is anemophilous (wind), and fertilisation does not require water. The resulting seed is "naked" (exposed on the cone scale, no fruit).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Male cone: microsporangium → microspore (n) → pollen (male gametophyte)
Female cone: ovule on scale → megaspore (n) → female gametophyte (archegonia)
Pollination: pollen → ovule (wind) → pollen tube → fertilisation (no water)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Gymnosperms produce SEEDS but NOT fruits; angiosperms produce both.  ·  The male cone produces pollen (male gametophyte); the female cone bears the ovule → seed.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects detailed Pinus male + female cone diagrams.  ·  The pollen structure (body + air-sac) and wind dispersal are key exam points.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Pinus male cone: microsporangium → microspore (n) → pollen grain (body + air-sac).  ·  Pinus female cone: ovule on the cone scale → archegonium → fertilisation → seed (naked).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Pinus is wind-pollinated (anemophilous); no flowers, no nectar, no insects involved.  ·  Gymnosperms do NOT undergo double fertilisation (angiosperm feature).

rows.text: Pinus: woody, needle-like leaves, cones; no flowers or fruits.  ·  Male cone: microsporangium → pollen (wind-dispersed).  ·  Female cone: ovule on the cone scale → seed (naked).  ·  Pollen: body + air-sac; two-celled; wind dispersal.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Gymnosperms appeared ~300 Ma (Carboniferous); they dominated the Mesozoic era.  ·  A single Pinus male cone can release millions of pollen grains for wind dispersal.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: DETAILED GYMNOSPERM (Pinus) MORPHOLOGY AND REPRODUCTION.  ·  Plant body: woody stem (trunk) + branch system; needle-like (Pinus) or scale-like (Deodar) leaves; no true flowers; reproduction via cones (strobili).  ·  Male cone (microstrobilus): small, clustered at the base of new shoots; microsporangia → microspores (n) → pollen grains (male gametophyte) with an air-sac for wind dispersal.
